cards.tip: FIX — After diagnosing the NV Energy power outage, offering 'Call me the moment your power returns and I'll come straight out to verify the unit fires back up' would have locked in an emergency callback they'd have accepted—that's the TGL you left on the table.

WIN — When a frustrated customer pushed back on being charged another $5k after a recent $4k repair, Joe said 'I'm not defending them—it's 45 degrees in February; compressors don't give fair warning,' which validated the concern while explaining technical reality, earning the diagnostic appointment.

FIX — When they said 'just get it fixed, whatever it takes,' lock in the estimate appointment time right then: 'I'll have findings in 2 hours and we'll meet right after to review all options'—so they don't second-guess while you're working.
WIN — When customers mentioned they couldn't sleep because the upstairs unit is loud at night, you pivoted to thermostat scheduling as the solution—that consultative approach is what flips calls.

WIN — Your tire analogy proved replacement was the only real fix, and offering to walk the in-laws through it directly got her buy-in to move forward with the structural fix and full system replacement.
FIX — When customer stated urgency ('just want to get it fixed'), schedule specialist visit for exact pricing instead of deferring to 'think about it'.
WIN — Clear diagnostics of blown capacitor and professional handling of customer
WIN — Effectively positioned replacement as best option vs accumulating repairs
FIX — Document decision clearly when power of attorney holder is involved
WIN: Thorough compressor diagnosis and R22 constraint explained; FIX: no customer commitment or next steps captured before call end
WIN — Navigated complex multi-component failure and R-22 obsolescence to recommend full system replacement
WIN — Thorough diagnosis with excellent rapport; clear explanation of rust risk leading to system replacement recommendation

WIN — Exceptional technical diagnosis with clear customer education on cascading failures

FIX — Inspection phase executed well with good discovery and clear system explanations; when presenting options later, address competitive context by emphasizing Sierra's systematic diagnostic advantage.

WIN — You nailed the skeptical flip by validating her 'salesy' concern upfront ("I definitely hear where you're coming from"), then layered options instead of pushing one. The Monday Comfort Advisor appointment closed because it felt consultative, not forced. Repeat that move.

FIX — When you present the recommendation, connect it to the exact thermostat problem the customer mentioned (78 degrees), and tell her the exact temperature she'll achieve—hearing 'here's how you get to 70 degrees' instead of 'your compressor is bad' is what gets the commitment.

FIX — David's 10-minute tangent about flooring jobs and his family ate critical time before the options presentation; once he explained the capacitor issue, he should have refocused with 'Let me get you a quote on that repair,' moving the call toward the close instead of extending the diagnosis with technical stories.

WIN — Your car-battery analogy ('flip the ignition, cranks that motor') made the motor start device click for the customer, and when you offered the free specialist consult ('doesn't cost anything for them to come out'), they said yes to the $557 install plus the follow-up visit.

FIX — When you discovered the wasp obstacle on the outdoor unit, acknowledge it to the customer before stepping away to call the office: 'There's wasps out there, but let me check with the office on how we can handle that' — that keeps them engaged in the evaluation instead of leaving them mid-inspection while you troubleshoot.
